## ESVS-grounded answer

According to ESVS guidelines, all recently symptomatic carotid stenosis patients scheduled to undergo carotid endarterectomy (CEA) should be prescribed antiplatelet therapy in the perioperative and long-term period (Recommendation 26). Early institution of antiplatelet therapy is specifically recommended for patients with >50% carotid stenosis and recent TIA or minor stroke awaiting CEA (Recommendation 12). The guidelines further recommend developing local protocols to specify preferred antiplatelet regimens (combination vs. monotherapy) for such cases, to avoid delay in urgent surgery (Recommendation 25). For patients with TIA or minor stroke and known atrial fibrillation and ipsilateral 50–99% carotid stenosis, a comprehensive neurovascular workup with multidisciplinary team review is recommended to determine whether urgent carotid revascularisation or anticoagulation alone is indicated (Recommendation 63). No guideline recommendation was identified regarding the interaction between perioperative anticoagulation (apixaban) for atrial fibrillation and perioperative antiplatelet therapy in this scenario (interaction_gap).

## Interpretation

Non-ESVS interpretation (clinical reasoning beyond the retrieved guideline text):
There is a clear guideline recommendation for perioperative antiplatelet therapy in recently symptomatic carotid stenosis patients scheduled for CEA, but no evidence-based guideline direction on how to safely reconcile this with concurrent anticoagulation (apixaban) for atrial fibrillation. The guidelines specifically call for multidisciplinary team review in cases like this, where both high thrombotic and bleeding risks must be balanced, and recommend local protocols. In practice, the details of perioperative anticoagulation management (e.g. holding apixaban prior to surgery, timing of restart, antiplatelet agent selection and timing) must be individualized and decided by the local neurovascular MDT. There is no ESVS-endorsed schedule for holding/restarting apixaban nor for combining it with antiplatelets around CEA. Addition of antiplatelet therapy is nevertheless guideline-mandated for this carotid indication; precise regimens and safety strategy remain subject to local multidisciplinary policy and the patient's individualized risk assessment.
